manifest.title: Gossiping and the Characterization by T-Graphs and M-Graphs

inputs.abstract:
In the Gossiping problem, the edges of a multigraph $G$ are calls between
participants, and one asks for an ordering of the calls, given by a labeling of
the edges with natural numbers, such that every participant learns the secret of
every other participant. Equivalently, the edge-labeled graph must be temporally
connected: for every ordered pair of vertices there is a path whose edge labels
strictly increase. We say that $G$ is *label-connected* if such a labeling exists.

This submission defines the problem and the two structural witnesses of the
classical characterization of label-connected multigraphs. A *$T$-graph* has two
spanning trees sharing at most one edge. An *$M$-graph* is not a $T$-graph but
contains a cycle of length at least four together with two edge-disjoint
spanning forests, each with exactly four components, all of which meet the cycle.
The main statement is that a finite multigraph is label-connected if and only if
it has at most one vertex, is a $T$-graph, or is an $M$-graph.

concepts.title: Characterization of Label-Connected Multigraphs

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Multigraphs are Mathlib's `Graph α β`; finiteness of the vertex set and of the

`M`-graphs are those of the concepts `Gossiping`, `TGraph` and `MGraph`. Loops are

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax630294.Gossiping
import Lax630294.TGraph
import Lax630294.MGraph

/-!
---
title: Characterization of Label-Connected Multigraphs
type: theorem
---

Let `G` be a finite multigraph. Then `G` is a yes-instance of Gossiping
(label-connected) if and only if at least one of the following holds:

1. `G` has at most one vertex;
2. `G` is a `T`-graph;
3. `G` is an `M`-graph.

# Formalization notes

Multigraphs are Mathlib's `Graph α β`; finiteness of the vertex set and of the
edge set is assumed. The definitions of label-connectedness, `T`-graphs and
`M`-graphs are those of the concepts `Gossiping`, `TGraph` and `MGraph`. Loops are
allowed in `G`; they play no role on either side of the equivalence.
-/

namespace Lax630294.Characterization

open Graph Lax630294.Gossiping Lax630294.TGraph Lax630294.MGraph

universe u v

/-- A finite multigraph is label-connected if and only if it has at most one vertex,
is a `T`-graph, or is an `M`-graph. -/
axiom isLabelConnected_iff {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (G : Graph α β)
    (hV : V(G).Finite) (hE : E(G).Finite) :
    IsLabelConnected G ↔ V(G).Subsingleton ∨ IsTGraph G ∨ IsMGraph G

end Lax630294.Characterization

statements.signature:
isLabelConnected_iff : ∀ {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (G : Graph α β),
  G.vertexSet.Finite →
    G.edgeSet.Finite →
      Iff (Lax630294.Gossiping.IsLabelConnected G)
        (Or G.vertexSet.Subsingleton (Or (Lax630294.TGraph.IsTGraph G) (Lax630294.MGraph.IsMGraph G)))

concepts.title: The Gossiping Problem
concepts.description:
Let `G` be a multigraph. A *labeling* assigns a natural number to every edge.
A *strict temporal path* from `u` to `v` is a path from `u` to `v` in `G` whose
edge labels strictly increase in traversal order; the path of length zero is
allowed. The labeled graph is *temporally connected* if, for every ordered pair
of vertices `u, v`, there is a strict temporal path from `u` to `v`. The instance
`G` of Gossiping is a *yes-instance* if some labeling makes `G` temporally
connected.

Interpreting each edge as a call between its endpoints and each label as the
time of the call, a labeling is an ordering of the calls, and it is temporally
connected exactly when every participant learns every secret.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Multigraphs are Mathlib's `Graph α β`, with vertex type `α` and edge type `β`;
parallel edges and loops are allowed, and `G.IsLink e x y` states that the edge
`e` has the ends `x` and `y`. Finiteness is not part of the definition and is
assumed where it matters. Loops never lie on a path, so they do not influence
the answer. Labels are taken in `ℕ`; only their relative order matters. A path
of length `k` is given by its `k + 1` pairwise distinct vertices `x 0, …, x k`
and its `k` edges `e 0, …, e (k - 1)`, where `e i` links `x i` and `x (i + 1)`.
A graph with at most one vertex is a yes-instance, since only paths of length
zero are required.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.Graph.Basic
import Mathlib.Order.Fin.Basic
import Mathlib.Order.Monotone.Basic

/-!
---
title: The Gossiping Problem
type: definition
---

Let `G` be a multigraph. A *labeling* assigns a natural number to every edge.
A *strict temporal path* from `u` to `v` is a path from `u` to `v` in `G` whose
edge labels strictly increase in traversal order; the path of length zero is
allowed. The labeled graph is *temporally connected* if, for every ordered pair
of vertices `u, v`, there is a strict temporal path from `u` to `v`. The instance
`G` of Gossiping is a *yes-instance* if some labeling makes `G` temporally
connected.

Interpreting each edge as a call between its endpoints and each label as the
time of the call, a labeling is an ordering of the calls, and it is temporally
connected exactly when every participant learns every secret.

# Formalization notes

Multigraphs are Mathlib's `Graph α β`, with vertex type `α` and edge type `β`;
parallel edges and loops are allowed, and `G.IsLink e x y` states that the edge
`e` has the ends `x` and `y`. Finiteness is not part of the definition and is
assumed where it matters. Loops never lie on a path, so they do not influence
the answer. Labels are taken in `ℕ`; only their relative order matters. A path
of length `k` is given by its `k + 1` pairwise distinct vertices `x 0, …, x k`
and its `k` edges `e 0, …, e (k - 1)`, where `e i` links `x i` and `x (i + 1)`.
A graph with at most one vertex is a yes-instance, since only paths of length
zero are required.
-/

namespace Lax630294.Gossiping

open Graph

variable {α β : Type*}

/-- A strict temporal path from `u` to `v` with respect to the labeling `ℓ`: a path
of some length `k` whose edge labels strictly increase along the path. -/
def HasTemporalPath (G : Graph α β) (ℓ : β → ℕ) (u v : α) : Prop :=
  ∃ (k : ℕ) (x : Fin (k + 1) → α) (e : Fin k → β),
    x 0 = u ∧ x (Fin.last k) = v ∧ Function.Injective x ∧
    (∀ i : Fin k, G.IsLink (e i) (x i.castSucc) (x i.succ)) ∧
    StrictMono (fun i => ℓ (e i))

/-- The labeling `ℓ` makes `G` temporally connected: every vertex reaches every
vertex by a strict temporal path. -/
def IsTemporallyConnected (G : Graph α β) (ℓ : β → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ u ∈ V(G), ∀ v ∈ V(G), HasTemporalPath G ℓ u v

/-- `G` is label-connected, i.e. a yes-instance of Gossiping: some labeling makes it temporally connected. -/
def IsLabelConnected (G : Graph α β) : Prop :=
  ∃ ℓ : β → ℕ, IsTemporallyConnected G ℓ

end Lax630294.Gossiping

concepts.title: M-Witness and M-Graph
concepts.description:
An *`M`-witness* of a multigraph `G` consists of pairwise edge-disjoint subgraphs
`C`, `F₁`, `F₂` of `G`, where `C` is a cycle of length at least four and each `Fᵢ`
is a spanning forest of `G` with exactly four components, each of which contains
a vertex of `C`. A multigraph *admits an `M`-witness* if it has one, and it is an
*`M`-graph* if it admits an `M`-witness and is not a `T`-graph.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Subgraphs are given by their edge sets, as in the concept of spanning forests.
The requirement that each component of `Fᵢ` contains a vertex of `C` is stated as:
every vertex of `G` is connected in `Fᵢ` to a vertex incident to an edge of `C`.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax630294.TGraph

/-!
---
title: M-Witness and M-Graph
type: definition
---

An *`M`-witness* of a multigraph `G` consists of pairwise edge-disjoint subgraphs
`C`, `F₁`, `F₂` of `G`, where `C` is a cycle of length at least four and each `Fᵢ`
is a spanning forest of `G` with exactly four components, each of which contains
a vertex of `C`. A multigraph *admits an `M`-witness* if it has one, and it is an
*`M`-graph* if it admits an `M`-witness and is not a `T`-graph.

# Formalization notes

Subgraphs are given by their edge sets, as in the concept of spanning forests.
The requirement that each component of `Fᵢ` contains a vertex of `C` is stated as:
every vertex of `G` is connected in `Fᵢ` to a vertex incident to an edge of `C`.
-/

namespace Lax630294.MGraph

open Graph Lax630294.SpanningStructures Lax630294.TGraph

variable {α β : Type*}

/-- `F` is a spanning forest of `G` with four components, each containing a vertex
of the cycle `C`. -/
def IsFourComponentForestMeeting (G : Graph α β) (C F : Set β) : Prop :=
  IsSpanningForest G F 4 ∧
    ∀ x : V(G), ∃ c : V(G), (c : α) ∈ incidentVertices G C ∧ (underlying G F).Reachable x c

/-- `C, F₁, F₂` is an `M`-witness of `G`. -/
def IsMWitness (G : Graph α β) (C F₁ F₂ : Set β) : Prop :=
  IsCycle G C ∧ 4 ≤ C.encard ∧
  IsFourComponentForestMeeting G C F₁ ∧ IsFourComponentForestMeeting G C F₂ ∧
  Disjoint C F₁ ∧ Disjoint C F₂ ∧ Disjoint F₁ F₂

/-- `G` admits an `M`-witness. -/
def AdmitsMWitness (G : Graph α β) : Prop :=
  ∃ C F₁ F₂ : Set β, IsMWitness G C F₁ F₂

/-- `G` is an `M`-graph: it admits an `M`-witness and is not a `T`-graph. -/
def IsMGraph (G : Graph α β) : Prop :=
  AdmitsMWitness G ∧ ¬ IsTGraph G

end Lax630294.MGraph

concepts.title: Cycles, Spanning Trees and Spanning Forests of a Multigraph
concepts.description:
Let `G` be a multigraph and let `F` be a set of edges of `G`; we identify `F`
with the spanning subgraph of `G` that keeps all vertices of `G` and only the
edges in `F`. The *components* of `F` are the connected components of this
subgraph; every vertex of `G` lies in a component, even if it is incident to no
edge of `F`.

A set `F` of edges is *simple* if it contains no loop and no two parallel edges.
A simple set `F` is *acyclic* if the subgraph it forms has no cycle, and it is a
*tree* if it is acyclic and connected. A *spanning tree* of `G` is a simple set of
edges of `G` forming a tree on all vertices of `G`. A *spanning forest with `k`
components* of `G` is a simple acyclic set of edges of `G` with exactly `k`
components.

A *cycle of length `n ≥ 1`* consists of `n` pairwise distinct vertices
`v₀, …, vₙ₋₁` and `n` pairwise distinct edges `e₀, …, eₙ₋₁` such that `eᵢ` joins
`vᵢ` and `vᵢ₊₁`, with indices taken modulo `n`. Its edge set is `{e₀, …, eₙ₋₁}`.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The multigraph is Mathlib's `Graph α β`. Connectivity, components, trees and
acyclicity are taken from Mathlib's theory of simple graphs, applied to
`Graph.toSimpleGraph` of the spanning subgraph `G.restrict F`; this forgets loops
and parallel edges. Requiring `(G.restrict F).Simple` restores them, so that a loop
or a pair of parallel edges in `F` is never accepted as part of a tree or a forest
(these are the cycles of length one and two). Cycles are given by an explicit cyclic
sequence indexed by `ZMod n`; a cycle of length one is a loop and a cycle of length
two is a pair of parallel edges. The number of components is an extended natural number (`ENat.card`), so
that infinitely many components are not mistaken for a finite number.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.Graph.Delete
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.Graph.Simple
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Data.ENat.Basic

/-!
---
title: Cycles, Spanning Trees and Spanning Forests of a Multigraph
type: definition
---

Let `G` be a multigraph and let `F` be a set of edges of `G`; we identify `F`
with the spanning subgraph of `G` that keeps all vertices of `G` and only the
edges in `F`. The *components* of `F` are the connected components of this
subgraph; every vertex of `G` lies in a component, even if it is incident to no
edge of `F`.

A set `F` of edges is *simple* if it contains no loop and no two parallel edges.
A simple set `F` is *acyclic* if the subgraph it forms has no cycle, and it is a
*tree* if it is acyclic and connected. A *spanning tree* of `G` is a simple set of
edges of `G` forming a tree on all vertices of `G`. A *spanning forest with `k`
components* of `G` is a simple acyclic set of edges of `G` with exactly `k`
components.

A *cycle of length `n ≥ 1`* consists of `n` pairwise distinct vertices
`v₀, …, vₙ₋₁` and `n` pairwise distinct edges `e₀, …, eₙ₋₁` such that `eᵢ` joins
`vᵢ` and `vᵢ₊₁`, with indices taken modulo `n`. Its edge set is `{e₀, …, eₙ₋₁}`.

# Formalization notes

The multigraph is Mathlib's `Graph α β`. Connectivity, components, trees and
acyclicity are taken from Mathlib's theory of simple graphs, applied to
`Graph.toSimpleGraph` of the spanning subgraph `G.restrict F`; this forgets loops
and parallel edges. Requiring `(G.restrict F).Simple` restores them, so that a loop
or a pair of parallel edges in `F` is never accepted as part of a tree or a forest
(these are the cycles of length one and two). Cycles are given by an explicit cyclic
sequence indexed by `ZMod n`; a cycle of length one is a loop and a cycle of length
two is a pair of parallel edges. The number of components is an extended natural number (`ENat.card`), so
that infinitely many components are not mistaken for a finite number.
-/

namespace Lax630294.SpanningStructures

open Graph

variable {α β : Type*}

/-- The simple graph underlying the spanning subgraph of `G` with edge set `F`. -/
abbrev underlying (G : Graph α β) (F : Set β) : SimpleGraph V(G) :=
  (G.restrict F).toSimpleGraph

/-- The vertices of `G` incident to an edge of `F`. -/
def incidentVertices (G : Graph α β) (F : Set β) : Set α :=
  {x | ∃ e ∈ F, G.Inc e x}

/-- `C` is the edge set of a cycle of `G` of some length `n ≥ 1`: there are
pairwise distinct vertices `v 0, …, v (n - 1)` and pairwise distinct edges
`e 0, …, e (n - 1)` such that `e i` links `v i` and `v (i + 1)`, with indices
taken modulo `n`, and `C` consists of these edges. Its length is `C.encard`. -/
def IsCycle (G : Graph α β) (C : Set β) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∃ (v : ZMod n → α) (e : ZMod n → β),
    Function.Injective v ∧ Function.Injective e ∧
    (∀ i, G.IsLink (e i) (v i) (v (i + 1))) ∧ Set.range e = C

/-- `T` is a spanning tree of `G`. -/
def IsSpanningTree (G : Graph α β) (T : Set β) : Prop :=
  T ⊆ E(G) ∧ (G.restrict T).Simple ∧ (underlying G T).IsTree

/-- `F` is a spanning forest of `G` with exactly `k` components. -/
def IsSpanningForest (G : Graph α β) (F : Set β) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  F ⊆ E(G) ∧ (G.restrict F).Simple ∧ (underlying G F).IsAcyclic ∧
    ENat.card (underlying G F).ConnectedComponent = k

end Lax630294.SpanningStructures

concepts.title: T-Graph
concepts.description:
A *`T`-witness* of a multigraph `G` is a pair of spanning trees of `G` that share
at most one edge. A multigraph is a *`T`-graph* if it has a `T`-witness.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The two trees are given by their edge sets `T₁` and `T₂`; they may coincide only
when they have at most one edge in common, that is, when `G` has at most two
vertices.

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax630294.SpanningStructures

/-!
---
title: T-Graph
type: definition
---

A *`T`-witness* of a multigraph `G` is a pair of spanning trees of `G` that share
at most one edge. A multigraph is a *`T`-graph* if it has a `T`-witness.

# Formalization notes

The two trees are given by their edge sets `T₁` and `T₂`; they may coincide only
when they have at most one edge in common, that is, when `G` has at most two
vertices.
-/

namespace Lax630294.TGraph

open Graph Lax630294.SpanningStructures

variable {α β : Type*}

/-- `T₁, T₂` are spanning trees of `G` sharing at most one edge. -/
def IsTWitness (G : Graph α β) (T₁ T₂ : Set β) : Prop :=
  IsSpanningTree G T₁ ∧ IsSpanningTree G T₂ ∧ (T₁ ∩ T₂).encard ≤ 1

/-- `G` is a `T`-graph: it has a `T`-witness. -/
def IsTGraph (G : Graph α β) : Prop :=
  ∃ T₁ T₂ : Set β, IsTWitness G T₁ T₂

end Lax630294.TGraph

sections.title: Strategy
sections.markdown:
Sufficiency: a `T`-witness or an `M`-witness is turned into a labeling by gathering secrets along
the first tree or forest, exchanging them (through a hub edge, or around the cycle), and distributing
them along the second one. Necessity: contract the maximal sets supporting two edge-disjoint spanning
trees, bound the number of calls in the quotient from below by `2r - 4`, split into the cases
`2r - 3` edges (a `T`-witness) and `2r - 4` edges (canonical form of the call order, a protected
extension of a four-cycle to an `M`-witness of the quotient, and a lift to the original graph through
a compatible choice of ports).
